title: Importance of shrinkage in empirical Bayes estimates for diagnostics in population pharmacokinetics

content.abstract_summary: Classic foundational paper on parameter shrinkage (eta-shrinkage and epsilon-shrinkage) in empirical Bayes estimates (EBEs) for nonlinear mixed-effects models. Demonstrates how shrinkage masks model misspecification, distorts covariate relationships, and leads to false conclusions in model evaluation.
key_findings: When individual data are uninformative (sparse sampling), EBEs shrink toward the population mean (eta-shrinkage) and individual residuals shrink toward zero (epsilon-shrinkage)
High shrinkage (>20–30%) renders standard diagnostic plots (e.g. EBE vs covariate, individual IPRED vs DV) misleading and incapable of detecting structural misspecification
Crucial for hybrid NLME-ML models: overparameterized neural network layers can artificially absorb individual variance, creating severe unnoticed shrinkage and spurious covariate relationships
Establishes formal mathematical equations for quantifying eta-shrinkage and epsilon-shrinkage
limitations: Focused on classical parametric NLME; implications for neural-ODE hybrid layers need formal mathematical extension

extracted_claims.text: Shrinkage is a well-known phenomenon in empirical Bayes estimation. High shrinkage conceals true model misspecification and distorts individual parameter-covariate relationships.

gaps_addressed: Provides foundational shrinkage theory for analyzing how neural network layers interact with between-subject variability in Pillar 1 (M1.2)

provenance.notes: Added 2026-08-29 by Antigravity review. Foundational reference for eta-shrinkage in mixed-effects hybrid models.
